verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच भगदत्तं धनञ्जयः। अनेनैव कृतं सर्वं भविष्यत्यनुजानता॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having been thus addressed by that exalted being (Krishna), and having seen Bhima and Arjuna standing there with cheerful face, Yudhishthira thus replied.

verses.sanskrit: तं विजित्य महाबाहुः कुन्तीपुत्रो धनञ्जयः। प्रययावुत्तरां तस्माद्दिशं धनदपालिताम्॥२॥
verses.english: Having thus conquered him, the mighty armed son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, then went towards the north, the direction presided over by the lord of wealth (Kubera).
verses.bhavadeepa: एवमिति अनेनैव करदानेनैव अनुजानता अनुज्ञां दत्तवता ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: अन्तर्गिरिं च कौन्तेयस्तथैव च बहिर्गिरिम्। तथैवोपगिरं चैव विजिग्ये पुरुषर्षभः॥३॥
verses.english: The son of Kunti, that best of men, conquered the inner-mountains, the outer mountains and the smaller mountains.

verses.sanskrit: विजित्य पर्वतान्सर्वान्ये च तत्र नराधिपाः। तान्वशे स्थापयित्वा स धनान्यादाय सर्वशः॥४॥
verses.english: Having conquered all the mountains and all the kings that lived on them and having brought them under his sway, he exacted tribute from them all.

verses.sanskrit: तैरेव सहितः सर्वैरनुरज्य च तान्नृपान्। उलूकवासिनं राजन्बृहन्तमुपजग्मिवान्॥५॥
verses.english: O king, having won the affection of those kings, and having united himself with them, he next marched against Brihanta (who was) the king of Uluka.

verses.sanskrit: मृदङ्गवरनादेन रथनेमिस्वनेन च। हस्तिनां च निनादेन कम्पयन्वसुधामिमाम्॥६॥
verses.english: Trembling the earth with the sound of his drums, with the clatter of his chariot wheels and with the roar of the elephants that were with his troops.

verses.sanskrit: ततो बृहन्तस्त्वरितो बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा। निष्क्रम्य नगरात्तस्माद्योधयामास फाल्गुनम्॥७॥
verses.english: Brihanta soon came out of his city with his five kinds of troops and gave battle to Falguni (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: सुमहान्सन्निपातोऽभूद्धनञ्जयबृहन्तयोः। न शशाक बृहन्तस्तु सोढुं पाण्डवविक्रमम्॥८॥
verses.english: The battle that took place between Brihanta and Dhananjaya was a terrible one. But Brihanta was not able to stand against the prowess of the son of Pandu (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: सोऽविषह्यतमं मत्वा कौन्तेयं पर्वतेश्वरः। उपावर्तत दुर्धर्षो रत्नान्यादाय सर्वशः॥९॥
verses.english: Thinking that the son of Kunti was incapable of being withstood, that invincible mountain-king came to him with all his wealth.

verses.sanskrit: स तद्राज्यमवस्थाप्य उलूकसहितो ययौ। सेनाबिन्दुमथो राजन्राज्यादाशु समाक्षिपत्॥१०॥
verses.english: O king, having made peace with him and having placed him in his kingdom, he (Arjuna) marched against Senabindu whom he expelled from his kingdom.

verses.sanskrit: मोदापुरं वामवेदं सुदामानं सुसङ्कुलम्। उलूकानुत्तरांश्चैव तांश्च राज्ञः समानयत्॥११॥
verses.english: He then subjugated Modapura, Vamadeva, Sudamana, Susankula, the northern Ulukas and the kings and the people of those countries.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रस्थः पुरुषैरेव धर्मराजस्य शासनात्। किरीटी जितवान्राजन्देशान्पञ्चगणांस्ततः॥१२॥
verses.english: O king, at the command of Yudhishthira, Kirti (Arjuna) brought under his sway all these five countries and their people by sending only his troops against them and not moving himself from the city (of Senavindu).

verses.sanskrit: स देवप्रस्थमासाद्य सेनाबिन्दोः पुरं प्रति। बलेन चतुरङ्गेण निवेशमकरोत्प्रभुः॥१३॥
verses.english: After his arrival at Devaprastha, the city of Senavindu, the lord (Arjuna) took up his quarters there with his five kinds of troops.

verses.sanskrit: स तैः परिवृतः सर्वैर्विष्वगश्वं नराधिपम्। अभ्यगच्छन्महातेजाः पौरवं पुरुषर्षभ॥१४॥
verses.english: Surrounded by the kings and all the people whom he subjugated, he marched against that best of men, the descendant of Puru, Vishvagashva.

verses.sanskrit: विजित्य चाहवे शूरान्पार्वतीयान्महारथान्। जिगाय सेनया राजन्पुरं पौरवरक्षितम्॥१५॥
verses.english: king, having subjugated in battle the brave mountaineers who were all great warriors, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) conquered with the help of his troops the city protected by the Puru King.

verses.sanskrit: पौरवं युधि निर्जित्य दस्यून्पर्वतवासिनः। गणानुत्सवसङ्केतानजयत्सप्त पाण्डवः॥१६॥
verses.english: Having vanquished the Puru king, and also the robber tribes of the mountains, the son of Pandu brought under his sway the seven tribes, called Utsavasanketa.

verses.sanskrit: ततः काश्मीरकान्वीरान्क्षत्रियान्क्षत्रियर्षभः। व्यजयल्लोहितं चैव मण्डलैर्दशभिः सह॥१७॥
verses.english: That best of Kshatriyas (Arjuna) then vanquished the brave Kshatriyas of Kashmira and also the king Lohita, as well as ten minor chiefs.
verses.bhavadeepa: उत्सवसंकेतान्‌  स्त्रीपुंसयोः परस्परप्रीतिरेव रत्यर्थं संकेतः न तु दांपत्यव्यवस्था पशूनामिव यत्रास्तीत्यर्थः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: ततस्त्रिगर्ताः कौन्तेयं दार्वाः कोकनदास्तथा। क्षत्रिया बहवो राजन्नुपावर्तन्त सर्वशः॥१८॥
verses.english: O king, then the Trigartas, the Danavas, the Kokanadas and various other Kshatriyas advanced against the son of Kunti.

verses.sanskrit: अभिसारीं ततो रम्यां विजिग्ये कुरुनन्दनः। उरगावासिनं चैव रोचमानं रणेऽजयत्॥१९॥
verses.english: That descendant of Kuru (Arjuna) then conquered the charming city, named Abhisari. He then vanquished Rochamana, who ruled in urga.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सिंहपुरं रम्यं चित्रायुधसुरक्षितम्। प्राधमद्बलमास्थाय पाकशासन्निराहवे॥२०॥
verses.english: The son of the chastiser of Paka (Arjuna) then conquered the charming city of Singhapura which was well protected by all kinds of weapons.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सुह्यांश्च चोलांश्च किरीटी पाण्डवर्षभः। सहितः सर्वसैन्येन प्रामथत्कुरुनन्दनः॥२१॥
verses.english: Then that best of the Pandavas the descendant of Kuru, Kirti (Arjuna) marched against the countries, called Sumba and Sumala, and attacked them.

verses.sanskrit: ततः परमविक्रान्तो बाह्लीकान्पाकशासनिः। महता परिमर्देन वशे चक्रे दुरासदान्॥२२॥
verses.english: Then after attacking with great force, the son of Indra (Arjuna), subjugated the Valhikas, ever difficult to vanquish.

verses.sanskrit: गृहीत्वा तु बलं सारं फल्गुनः पाण्डुनन्दनः। दरदान्सह काम्भोजैरजयत्पाकशासनिः॥२३॥
verses.english: The son of Pandu, and the son of Indra, Falguni (Arjuna), then took with him a select force and defeated the Daradas along with the Kambojas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रागुत्तरं दिशं ये च वसन्त्याश्रित्य दस्यवः। निवसन्ति वने ये च तान्सर्वानजयत्प्रभुः॥२४॥
verses.english: The lord (Arjuna) vanquished the robber tribes that lived in the north eastern frontier, and those also that lived in the forest.

verses.sanskrit: लोहान्परमकाम्भोजानृषिकानुत्तरानपि। सहितांस्तान्महाराज व्यजयत्पाकशासनिः॥२५॥
verses.english: O great king, the son of Indra also subjugated the allied tribes of the Lokas, the eastern Kambojas and the northern Rishikas.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषिकेष्वपि सङ्ग्रामे बभूवातिभयङ्करः। तारकामयसङ्काशः परस्त्वृषिकपार्थयोः॥२६॥
verses.english: The battle with the Rishikas was very fearful. The battle that took place between them and the son of Pritha (Arjuna) was equal to the between the gods and the Danavas, the immediate cause of which was Taraka (the wife of Brihaspati).

verses.sanskrit: स विजित्य ततो राजन्नृषिकान्रणमूर्धनि। शुकोदरसमांस्तत्र हयानष्टौ समानयत्॥२७॥
verses.english: O king, having vanquished the Rishikas on the field of battle, he took from them as tribute eight horses that were of the colour of the parrot's breast.

verses.sanskrit: मयूरसदृशानन्यानुत्तरानपरानपि। जवनानाशुगांश्चैव करार्थं समुपानयत्॥२८॥
verses.english: And some other horses also which had the colour of peacocks, these horses were all born in northern and other countries, and possessed great speed.

verses.sanskrit: स विनिर्जित्य सङ्ग्रामे हिमवन्तं सनिष्कृटम्। श्वेतपर्वतमासाद्य न्यविशत्पुरुषर्षभः॥२९॥
verses.english: Thus having conquered all the Himalayas and the Nishkuta mountains, he at last arrived at the white mountains and encamped on it.
verses.bhavadeepa: जवनान्‌ धावने शीघ्रान्‌ आशुगान्  यदृच्छया चलनसमर्थान् ॥२८॥
